title: The Maze With a Waiting Line
premise: A search robot wants the shortest route through an unweighted tile maze, but repeatedly chases the most tempting corridor. Expanding a first-in-first-out frontier one layer at a time finds a shortest route.
hook: Which square should the robot visit next?
visible_action: Tile coordinates enter and leave a visible queue; distance rings spread outward before the final path lights.
intended_takeaway_or_theme: Breadth-first search explores unweighted routes in increasing edge count.
gate: Keep every edge equal in cost and distinguish exploration from the final route.

style_application.material: Clean paths with optional original paper texture
style_application.why: The frontier and waiting queue stay visible together, so search order can be checked.
style_application.check: Verify every visited node, legal edge and queue operation.

editorial_pick.original_reason: A queue-based search can become a real visual trace rather than a vague coding analogy.
editorial_pick.proposed_first_version: Use one fixed maze, a visible waiting queue and an identified search token. Reveal the visited frontier in order.
editorial_pick.gate: Check the algorithm trace, legal connections and stopping rule against a deterministic reference.
